_what: Ground truth for the twenty cat photographs, labelled by eye on 2026-08-30 because manifest.json labels only the category (cat/dog/blurry/…) and nothing about the animal. Without this there is no way to say whether an on-device trait reader works — only whether it runs.
_who: Labelled from the photographs themselves, at thumbnail and full size. One person, one pass, no second opinion, so treat a single disagreement as a tie rather than as a failure.
_vocabulary: Exactly CatTraits.Allowed. base_color: ginger|grey|black|white|cream|brown. pattern: solid|tabby|bicolor|calico|tuxedo|pointed. fur_length: short|long.
_confidence: high — an unambiguous cat. low — I could argue the other way, and a reader that disagrees here has not necessarily failed. Score the high ones; report the low ones separately rather than folding them into one percentage.
_known_bias: Twelve of the twenty are tabbies. That is not a sampling choice, it is what a random pull of pet photographs looks like, and it means a reader that answers 'tabby' to everything scores 60% on pattern. Judge pattern by BOTH classes, never by the total.
_today: The shipped code answers 'solid' to all twenty and 'short' to all twenty, because CatTraits.FromColourOnly hard-codes both. So the bar to beat on pattern is 8/20, and it is 8/20 for a reason that has nothing to do with reading photographs.

cats.note: Black with a white bib and a white muzzle stripe. A reader that says tuxedo instead of solid is defensible — the white is exactly a tuxedo's.
Grey and white, no banding anywhere. bicolor is the better answer if the reader offers it.
A very dark chocolate cat on a red background. Black is arguable and the red cast makes it worse. Do not score this one against a reader that says black.
Calico, and the photograph has a heavy blue cast. Base colour of a calico is not a well-formed question in a six-colour palette.
A pale ginger tabby with a lot of white. cream is arguable for the base.
Calico kitten, same objection as cat_06. A human hand is in the frame and will be inside any mask that is not tight.
Dilute tortoiseshell with white. Neither the base nor the pattern maps cleanly onto this palette.
Coat is fluffier than the others here; long is arguable and I would not fault a reader for it.
Shot against a dark background under warm light — the case that pushes a frame-centre mean towards ginger.
A textbook tuxedo kitten. solid plus white markings is an equally true description of the same animal.
The one plausible long-hair in the set, and even here it is medium rather than long. A fur-length reader has almost nothing to learn from twenty photographs with one positive.
TWO kittens in the frame. Both are grey tabbies so the labels hold, but any mask will take both or pick one arbitrarily. Useful as a robustness case, not as an accuracy case.

owner_cats.note: The owner's own cat. Grey-brown tabby, clearly banded. brown is arguable for the base; tabby is not arguable.
Exotic shorthair, brown and cream. The shipped code answers ginger here, which is the miss that started this work.
White long-haired cat outdoors. cream is arguable for the base — the current estimate says cream and that is not a failure. The shipped code answers short, and that IS one.
